peek: The treasure money: ten thousand Pokos clears the company's debt.
full_text: There is no day limit in Pikmin 2: the goal is ten thousand Pokos of treasure to clear the company's debt. Treasures and enemy bodies both pay.

peek: The hovering hive that matches a Pikmin colour and grows your squad.
full_text: Pikmin multiply through their Onion, the hovering hive that matches their colour. Carrying a pellet or a defeated enemy's corpse back to the matching-colour Onion produces new seeds, usually in far larger numbers from a corpse.

peek: Found only in certain caves, they shrug off every hazard.
full_text: Bulbmin are found only in certain caves, and they shrug off every hazard. They cannot leave with you.

peek: Heavy, strong Pikmin that weigh as much as ten.
full_text: Purples weigh as much as ten Pikmin, so one lifts what ten would, and some treasures are impossible without them. Their landing on an enemy stuns it and they hit hard, but they are slow and fly low when thrown.

peek: The fastest Pikmin, poison-proof and able to dig up buried treasure.
full_text: White Pikmin are the fastest, are immune to poison, and can dig up treasure that is completely buried, which no other colour can find. Anything that eats one is poisoned.

peek: Where Purple and White Pikmin come from, only in caves.
full_text: Purple and White Pikmin come only from candypop buds in caves, in limited numbers. Treat them as tools rather than an army and keep them out of the front line.

peek: A spray that turns every enemy near you to stone for about nine seconds.
full_text: The purple ultra-bitter spray, made from ten purple berries from a Burgeoning Spiderwort or a found dose, turns every enemy near you to stone for about nine seconds, bomb rocks included. It is the answer to anything you cannot outfight, and the purple-berry plants are rarer than the red ones, so hoard it.

peek: A spray made from ten red berries that sends your Pikmin into a frenzy.
full_text: The red ultra-spicy spray, made from ten red berries, sends your Pikmin into a frenzy, faster and stronger, and flowers them. Nectar also flowers Pikmin, on its own.

peek: A drink that flowers a Pikmin so it runs and carries faster.
full_text: Nectar drops from eggs, rubble, nectar weed and some insects, and it flowers a Pikmin on its own. A flowered Pikmin runs and carries noticeably faster than a leaf, so let a new batch drink before a long carry.

peek: An enemy that fires mortars from range, some from towers.
full_text: Gatling Groinks fire mortars from range, some from towers you cannot reach. A dead one left lying gets back up.

peek: Pressing a shoulder button or Z just before landing halves your landing lag.
full_text: L-cancelling means pressing a shoulder button or Z within seven frames of landing during an air attack. The landing animation then plays twice as fast, halving your lag.

peek: Air-dodging diagonally into the ground to slide a short way.
full_text: To wavedash, air-dodge diagonally into the ground and you slide a short way while able to do any grounded action. It is how spacing and shield pressure work at a high level, and Luigi slides furthest, then the Ice Climbers and Mewtwo.

peek: A low jump made by releasing jump during the crouch before it.
full_text: A short hop is done by releasing jump during the crouch before it. It keeps aerials low and fast.

peek: Tapping down while falling to end a jump early.
full_text: Fast falling is a tap down while falling. It ends a jump early and beats an opponent's timing.

peek: Tapping the stick during the freeze to slide a small distance.
full_text: Tap the stick during the freeze itself and you slide a small distance each tap, which is how you escape multi-hit moves. It is a separate trick from DI, where you hold the stick during the freeze frames before you are launched to shift your angle.

peek: A shoulder-button press just before hitting a surface while tumbling.
full_text: When you are about to hit the ground, a wall, or a ceiling while tumbling, press a shoulder button within twenty frames to tech. You bounce up briefly untouchable instead of lying there, and a tech left or right rolls you away.

peek: Dropping off the ledge, then jumping and air-dodging back on.
full_text: Grabbing the ledge gives you invincible frames, and the ledge dash keeps some of them while skipping the slow climb animation. You drop off, then jump and air-dodge back on at the right moment.

peek: A hit straight down, the cleanest kill off stage.
full_text: Meteor smashes hit straight down and are the cleanest kills off stage. You can cancel one by jumping or using your up special eight frames after the hit stops, which is your escape when it happens to you.

peek: Going after or waiting for someone who has been knocked off the stage.
full_text: Most stocks are taken off the stage, not on it. When someone is knocked off, hit them again, or take the ledge yourself so they cannot grab it, which forces them onto the stage where you are waiting.

peek: Pressing attack while shielding to grab an opponent.
full_text: The shield grab is the standard punish: press attack while shielding. It skips the delay of dropping the shield and catches an opponent stuck in the end of their move.

peek: Hold the gas as the lights change from red to blue.
full_text: Hold the gas as the lights change from red to blue for a rocket start. Too early and you spin your tyres and leave slower than everyone.

peek: A speed boost charged by wiggling the stick while drifting.
full_text: Hop and hold to drift, then wiggle the stick side to side while sliding: the smoke goes white, yellow, then orange, and letting go on orange gives a mini-turbo. Later Mario Kart games make this time-based instead, so the wiggling motion is deliberate here.

peek: A blue shell for fourth place or lower that homes on the leader.
full_text: The blue Spiny Shell only comes to fourth place or lower. It runs along the ground with a siren, homes on the leader, flips anyone in its path, and can be held behind your kart to block other shells before you fire it.

peek: An upside-down question mark that launches whoever hits it.
full_text: Fake Item Boxes belong to first and second place. They look like an upside-down question mark, launch whoever hits them, and block incoming shells.

peek: The reward for gold in all four cups at 150cc, with every course mirrored.
full_text: Extra mode is the reward for earning gold in all four cups at 150cc, and it flips every course horizontally, so a corner that used to bend right now bends left. The title screen changes once it is unlocked, which is the easiest way to check you earned it.

peek: A handicap that lets computer racers recover from hits and catch back up.
full_text: The computer racers in 150cc and Extra lean harder on rubber-banding than in the easier classes. Expect one or two of them to receive a large handicap that lets them recover from being hit and catch back up quickly, so a comfortable lead near the finish line is not as safe as it looks.

peek: What you become in Battle Mode after losing all three balloons.
full_text: Losing all three balloons in Battle Mode turns you into a small, remote-controlled Bomb Kart that can still be attacked and stunned by other players' items. If it collides with anyone it explodes and you are out for good.

peek: A pre-made time set by the developers on three of the courses.
full_text: Three of the eight courses carry a staff ghost set by the developers, each raced by the character the course is themed around. They are the only pre-made times in the game; the other five courses have no staff record to chase.

peek: A button press at the right moment for extra damage.
full_text: Every attack has an action command, a button press at the right moment for extra damage. Landing it also earns Star Power faster.

peek: A tight-window B press that blocks a hit completely.
full_text: Press B in a tiny window as an enemy attack lands to superguard it for no damage and a point back. It is the harder version of a regular guard, so it is worth drilling on a weak, predictable enemy before relying on it in a fight that matters.

peek: The audience-fed resource spent on Crystal Star moves.
full_text: Every jump, hammer and partner attack earns Star Power for the Crystal Star moves, and it comes faster when you land the action command or add a Stylish move. You can also Appeal to gain Star Power directly while anyone is awake in the seats.

peek: An extra press at the right beat of an attack that makes the crowd cheer.
full_text: A Stylish move is an extra press at the right beat of the attack animation that makes the crowd cheer. It works only on normal and badge attacks, not items or counters.

peek: What each badge costs to wear; level-ups can give you more.
full_text: Each badge costs badge points to wear, so BP at level-up is often the best pick. Levelling up every hundred star points gives a choice of five HP, five FP or three badge points.

peek: A badge that only works while you are in Danger at five HP or less.
full_text: Power Rush, Close Call and Last Stand are badges people build around, and they only work while you are in Danger at five HP or less. Mega Rush works at exactly one HP, which is why some players have Chet Rippo lower their maximum HP on purpose.

peek: Forty-two sprites hidden in blocks; three buy a partner rank.
full_text: Forty-two Shine Sprites are hidden in blocks across the world. Merlon next to Professor Frankly trades three of them for a partner rank, each of the seven partners can go up twice, and Merluvlee the fortune teller will point you at the ones you missed.

peek: A bulletin board of odd jobs on the east side of Rogueport.
full_text: The Trouble Center on the east side of Rogueport is a bulletin board of odd jobs that pay coins, items and badges. It is part of Rogueport's side content, along with the Shine Sprites and the Pit of a Hundred Trials.

peek: A hundred floors of fights under Rogueport.
full_text: Under Rogueport lies the Pit of a Hundred Trials: a hundred floors of fights with Charlieton selling supplies part-way down. The enemy at the bottom coughs up the Return Postage badge.

peek: An Ultra Boots field move that grabs onto pipes and bars.
full_text: The Ultra Boots add a Spring Jump that grabs onto pipes and bars out of normal jumping range. It lets you back into areas that looked finished the first time through.

peek: The move you get by running and jumping three times.
full_text: To triple jump, run and jump three times. It is one of the moves the game is built around, and the red Wing Cap lets you start flying from a triple jump or a cannon shot.

peek: Run, then crouch and jump.
full_text: To long jump, run, then crouch and jump. It is one of the moves the game is built around, along with the triple jump, the wall kick, the backflip and the side flip.

peek: Jump into a wall and jump again.
full_text: To wall kick, jump into a wall and jump again. It is one of the moves the game is built around, along with the triple jump, the long jump, the backflip and the side flip.

peek: Press crouch while in the air.
full_text: To ground-pound, press crouch in the air. It is how you hurt the Whomp King: ground-pound his back three times while he is down.

peek: Mario's health, shown as an eight-wedge meter.
full_text: Health is the eight-wedge power meter, refilled by coins, spinning hearts, or surfacing in water. A hit from Eyerok costs three wedges.

peek: A red cap that lets you fly.
full_text: The red Wing Cap lets you fly from a triple jump or a cannon shot, slowly losing height. Like every cap, it only appears in courses once its switch has been hit, and it lasts sixty seconds.

peek: A green cap that makes you invulnerable and very heavy.
full_text: The green Metal Cap makes you invulnerable and very heavy: you sink and walk along the bottom, never need to breathe, and cannot swim. A metal Mario cannot be knocked back, so wearing it before a Bully fight in Lethal Lava Land removes the fall risk.

peek: A blue cap that turns you into a ghost for a short time.
full_text: The blue Vanish Cap makes you a ghost for a short time, walking through enemies and metal fences. Dire, Dire Docks is the one place you can wear metal and vanish at once.

peek: A fast, half-invisible imp that is new to Doom 64.
full_text: The nightmare imp is a translucent blue-purple imp, twice as fast as the ordinary kind, and it throws purple fireballs that fly twice as fast too. It is still an imp in health, so the shotgun handles it; the danger is the pack and the speed, not the toughness.

peek: The one new gun in Doom 64, a demonic laser that eats cells.
full_text: The Unmaker is the one new gun in Doom 64, a demonic laser that eats cells. It is found first in the secret level Outpost Omega, and on its own it is a slower, stronger plasma gun.

peek: Three hidden keys that power up the Unmaker.
full_text: There are three Demon Keys, one hidden on each of the secret levels Outpost Omega, The Lair and In The Void. Each one powers up the Unmaker (faster firing, then a second beam, then a third), and the keys also disable the three monster teleporters in the final level.

peek: A coloured key that opens every door of its colour on a level.
full_text: A locked door will not open until you are carrying a keycard or skull key of the matching colour, and once picked up a key opens every door of that colour on the level. Keys are lost the moment you leave a level, so there is no point carrying one forward.

peek: Hidden levels that hold the game's real reward.
full_text: Doom 64 has four secret levels, and they hide the game's real reward. Three of them, Outpost Omega, The Lair and In The Void, each hide a Demon Key that powers up the Unmaker.

peek: The 2020 re-release's extra episode, played after the ending.
full_text: The Lost Levels is the 2020 re-release's extra episode: six levels that start you stranded with no weapons on a distant base and end in Final Judgement, plus one separate fun level. It opens when you beat the final boss, or by finishing the secret level Hectic and using the Features menu's level select.
